request: why does pressing a guitar string halfway make the note an octave higher?

beats.intent: A long string stretched between two posts vibrating as one arch, 110 Hz
beats.narration: An open string vibrates as one long arch. This one plays a low A, a hundred and ten vibrations a second.
beats.code:
stage.title("Strings and octaves")
L = 8
post1 = Line([-4, 0.4, 0], [-4, 1.6, 0], color=GREY_B, stroke_width=6)
post2 = Line([4, 0.4, 0], [4, 1.6, 0], color=GREY_B, stroke_width=6)
t = ValueTracker(0)
string = always_redraw(lambda: FunctionGraph(lambda x: 1.0 + 0.45 * np.sin(PI * (x + 4) / L) * np.cos(t.get_value()),
                                               x_range=[-4, 4], color=YELLOW))
stage.add(post1, post2, string)
stage.play(t.animate.set_value(4 * TAU), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
stage.label(post2, "110 Hz", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: A second string pressed at its middle, vibrating as a shorter arch at 220 Hz
beats.narration: Press it at the middle and only half the string vibrates. The half-length arch shakes twice as fast: two hundred and twenty.
beats.code:
t2 = ValueTracker(0)
post3 = Line([-4, -2.2, 0], [-4, -1.0, 0], color=GREY_B, stroke_width=6)
fret = Line([0, -2.2, 0], [0, -1.0, 0], color=RED, stroke_width=6)
dead = Line([0, -1.6, 0], [4, -1.6, 0], color=GREY_B)
half = always_redraw(lambda: FunctionGraph(lambda x: -1.6 + 0.45 * np.sin(PI * (x + 4) / 4) * np.cos(t2.get_value()),
                                             x_range=[-4, 0], color=ORANGE))
stage.add(post3, fret, dead, half)
stage.play(t2.animate.set_value(8 * TAU), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
stage.label(fret, "220 Hz", direction=UP, color=ORANGE)

beats.intent: Bars of frequency for full, half and quarter length: 110, 220, 440 Hz
beats.narration: Halve it again for four hundred and forty. Every halving doubles the pitch: that doubling is what we hear as an octave.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
b = draw_bars(stage, [110, 220, 440], labels=["full", "half", "quarter"], color=ORANGE)
stage.caption("frequency in Hz: half the length, twice the pitch")

request: how do I change a recipe for 4 people into one for 6?

beats.intent: Bars of a recipe for 4: flour 200 g, sugar 100 g, butter 80 g
beats.narration: A cake for four uses two hundred grams of flour, a hundred of sugar and eighty of butter.
beats.code:
stage.title("Scaling a recipe")
b = draw_bars(stage, [200, 100, 80], labels=["flour", "sugar", "butter"])
stage.caption("serves 4")

beats.intent: The bars beside the scale factor 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5
beats.narration: Six people is one and a half times four, so every amount is multiplied by one point five.

beats.intent: Bars for 6 people: flour 300 g, sugar 150 g, butter 120 g, next to the old ones
beats.narration: Flour becomes three hundred grams, sugar a hundred and fifty, butter a hundred and twenty. The proportions stay the same.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
b2 = draw_bars(stage, [200, 300, 100, 150, 80, 120], labels=["flour 4", "flour 6", "sugar 4", "sugar 6", "butter 4", "butter 6"], color=GREEN)
stage.caption("serves 6: every amount × 1.5")

beats.intent: Sunlight entering a band of atmosphere, with blue light bouncing off in all directions
beats.narration: Sunlight is a mix of all colours. As it passes through the air, tiny molecules scatter some of it sideways.
beats.code:
stage.title("Why the sky is blue")
sun = Circle(radius=0.6, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to([-5.3, 1.8, 0])
air = Rectangle(width=11, height=2.2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.1).move_to([0.6, -0.4, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(sun), FadeIn(air))
stage.add(sun, air)
beam = Arrow([-4.7, 1.4, 0], [5.5, -1.2, 0], buff=0, color=WHITE)
stage.play(GrowArrow(beam))
stage.add(beam)
rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
blips = []
for k in range(8):
    p = np.array([-3 + k * 1.1, 1.4 - (k * 1.1 + 1.7) * 0.255, 0])
    ang = rng.uniform(0, TAU)
    blips.append(Arrow(p, p + 0.9 * np.array([np.cos(ang), np.sin(ang), 0]), buff=0, color=BLUE, stroke_width=3))
stage.play(*[GrowArrow(a) for a in blips])
stage.add(*blips)

beats.intent: Bars of how strongly each colour is scattered: red 1, blue about 6
beats.narration: Short blue waves scatter far more than long red ones, nearly six times as much. So blue light reaches your eyes from every part of the sky.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
b = draw_bars(stage, [1, 5.9], labels=["red 700 nm", "blue 450 nm"], color=BLUE)
stage.caption("scattering: blue about 6 times red")

beats.narration: Scattering goes as one over the wavelength to the fourth power: seven hundred over four hundred and fifty, to the fourth, is about five point nine.

request: how does the moon cause tides?

beats.intent: The Earth with an ocean layer around it and the Moon off to the right
beats.narration: The Earth is wrapped in oceans. The Moon, off to one side, pulls on everything.
beats.code:
stage.title("Tides")
earth = Circle(radius=1.2, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to([-1.5, -0.3, 0])
ocean = Circle(radius=1.55, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.35).move_to(earth.get_center()).set_z_index(-1)
moon = Circle(radius=0.35, color=GREY_B, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to([4.8, -0.3, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(ocean), FadeIn(earth), FadeIn(moon))
stage.add(ocean, earth, moon)
stage.label(moon, "Moon", direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: Pull arrows: longest on the near side, medium at the centre, shortest on the far side
beats.narration: The pull is strongest on the side facing the Moon and weakest on the far side.
beats.code:
c = earth.get_center()
arrows = [Arrow(c + x * RIGHT, c + x * RIGHT + L * RIGHT, buff=0, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=8,
                max_stroke_width_to_length_ratio=20, max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.4).set_z_index(3)
          for x, L in ((1.55, 1.8), (0, 1.2), (-1.55, 0.7))]
stage.play(*[GrowArrow(a) for a in arrows])
stage.add(*arrows)
stage.caption("stronger pull on the near side")

beats.intent: The ocean stretched into an oval with bulges toward and away from the Moon, labelled high tide
beats.narration: That difference stretches the oceans into an oval: one bulge toward the Moon, one on the far side. As the Earth turns under them, each coast gets two high tides a day.
beats.code:
bulge = Ellipse(width=3.9, height=2.7, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.35).move_to(c).set_z_index(-1)
stage.play(Transform(ocean, bulge), *[FadeOut(a) for a in arrows])
stage.add(ocean)
hi1 = Dot(c + 1.95 * RIGHT, color=WHITE)
hi2 = Dot(c + 1.95 * LEFT, color=WHITE)
stage.add(hi1, hi2)
stage.label(hi1, "high", direction=UP, color=WHITE)
stage.label(hi2, "high", direction=UP, color=WHITE)
stage.caption("two bulges: two high tides a day")
